text:
Aisha Khan: Drafting a concise rollout playbook for multi-variant fallbacks — want input before I turn this into a formal launch checklist. High level: feature flags + canaries + lightweight A/B for quality, staged regions, and automated fallback to cheaper/smaller model variants if errors or latency spike. Thoughts?

Tom Reynolds: +1. Need clear canary SLOs and automatic thresholds. Propose start at 1% traffic for 24h, then 5% for 12h, then 25% if stable.

Sophie Lee: Agree on staging. Also call out region sequencing: us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 -> ap-southeast-1. Keep strict circuit-breaker per-region to avoid blast radius.

Miguel Santos: For A/B quality checks, can we run a side-by-side scoring job on a sample of production traffic? We should capture n-gram overlap and hallucination rate heuristics.

Aisha Khan: Yup. Proposal includes a background evaluator that compares chosen metrics against baseline (prod model). If drift > X then auto-fallback. Need to set X. Suggestions?

Priya Nair: For latency SLOs I suggest 95th <= 350ms for short prompts. If 95th latency increases > 30% over baseline for more than 10m, trigger fallback. For error rate, >0.5% 5xx over 10m should also fallback.

Tom Reynolds: +1 to Priya. Also add token-cost delta threshold — if cost per request increases > 40% fallback.

Sophie Lee: Feature flag implementation detail: one flag for rollout (on/off), plus a param for variant routing: {"variant_order": ["v1","v2","safe"], "canary_pct": 1}. We'll need the console to edit canary_pct live.

Aisha Khan: Draft config snippet I'm thinking of:
```json
{
  "flag": "multi_variant_rollout",
  "variants": ["prod-v2", "prod-v1", "safe-quantized"],
  "canary_schedule": [1,5,25],
  "metrics": {
    "latency_p95_threshold_pct": 30,
    "error_rate_threshold": 0.005,
    "cost_increase_threshold_pct": 40
  },
  "fallback_policy": "last-stable"
}
```

Miguel Santos: That looks good. For the A/B portion we should sample 5% of canary traffic and mirror to offline evaluator for quality scoring. Keep user-visible experience tied to the primary variant.

Priya Nair: Ops note: need rate-limited rollback window to avoid flip-flopping. 5m cooldown after a fallback before reattempt. Also add annotation/logging for audit + operator action.

Tom Reynolds: How about telemetry: per-variant metrics by route, token_count histograms, and sample outputs for failing requests. We should tie regression alerts to the eval harness and not just raw metrics.

Sophie Lee: Also document behavior when region-specific capacity is low: route to next region with policy "prefer-region" vs "global-fallback". Default should be prefer-region then fallback to safe variant, not to another region unless the customer allows cross-region failover.

Aisha Khan: Good point. We'll add two toggles: allow_cross_region_failover (default false) and allow_safe_variant_fallback (default true).

deploy-bot: deployment pipeline note — canary releases will use blue/green for model artifacts and a config rollout for flags. CI will block if unit tests + perf tests fail.

Miguel Santos: Launch criteria checklist draft: 1) Console flag control + live canary edit; 2) Per-variant telemetry + evaluator in place; 3) Auto-fallback rules implemented; 4) Run 3 internal canaries with synthetic & shadow traffic; 5) Docs & runbook; 6) Graceful rollback tested.

Aisha Khan: Nice checklist. For product prioritization: do we treat this as part of the Dedicated roadmap (enterprise demand) or core Redwood API (ship to hosted customers)? My read: core API first, then Dedicated-specific config knobs (tenant isolation).

Tom Reynolds: Core API first is fine, but ensure RBAC and tenant isolation hooks are in the design so Dedicated teams can pick it up without rework.

Sophie Lee: We'll need a small UX for the console: a single page to edit rollout params + per-variant health. I can mock up a minimal design by next week.

Priya Nair: Runbook should include manual override steps, SLA impact communication template, and who to page for urgent rollbacks. I volunteer to draft the runbook section for on-call.

Aisha Khan: Perfect. I'll consolidate all feedback and push a follow-up doc with explicit numerical thresholds and the launch checklist. Aim to have a final playbook by EOD Friday. If anyone objects to any threshold call it out here.

Tom Reynolds: No objections from eng.

Miguel Santos: No objections from product QA. Will coordinate evaluator tests.

Sophie Lee: No objections from design.

Priya Nair: No objections from on-call. I'll add the escalation matrix tomorrow.

Aisha Khan: Thanks team :rocket: — I'll post the draft link when ready and tag for final review.
